justifications.problem-significance: The project tackles the genuinely hard problem of turning broad, historically important biological propositions into traceable formal statements and empirical tests across organisms. The frozen snapshot spans 1,763 claims, 91 proved mathematical statements, 174 data-tested claims and an organism inventory of 1,036 matched taxa (captured/mcp-overview.json, captured/mcp-tests-summary.json, captured/mcp-organisms.json). This is scientifically consequential because it explicitly separates proof from biological truth and exposes nulls, refutations and untestable claims, but the scope is diffuse: 1,522 claims are still neither proved nor tested, many source claims are historical rather than current frontier hypotheses, and issue #42's flying-fish program is primarily a plan rather than a completed scientific result (captured/github-issues.json).
justifications.scientific-impact: There are real, checkable results rather than only infrastructure: 174 unique claims have data verdicts (93 supports, 37 mixed, 30 refutes, 14 inconclusive), 90 use organism data, and 91 mathematical claims are recorded as proved, including 73 Lean-checked results (captured/mcp-tests-summary.json, captured/mcp-overview.json, captured/lean-reports.txt). The cell-geometry work found a consequential segmenter-bias null and downgraded a prior conclusion, while plant hygromorph work combines Lean statements with a small real-organism bilayer test (captured/github-issues.json issues #68, #69 and #81). Impact is capped because most tests are computational or historical reproductions, biological generality is often weak, only 33 of 174 tested claims have the independent faithfulness gate, and 5 of those were judged not representative with 6 contested (repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md).
justifications.decentralized-agency: The snapshot shows substantial distribution of labor and capability: 101 local chats, 262 subagents, 19 cloud agents, multiple model providers, distinct extraction, assessment, formalization, testing and red-team roles, and durable handoffs through files, issues and nanopublications (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md, repo/chats/README.md, captured/subagent-sessions.txt). Agents also triggered revisions after independent objections, including the segmenter-bias correction recorded in issues #68 and #69 (captured/github-issues.json). This is not a 10 because team roles and work packages were often centrally assigned by a human or lead issue (#53), the emperor/king/queen organization is partly simulation or design rather than demonstrated autonomous governance (repo/chats/SWARM_COORDINATION.md), and the internal forum snapshot has only one registered agent, no comments and four open requests (captured/forum-feed.json, captured/forum-requests.json).
justifications.collective-capability: A direct four-arm comparison is present and pre-registered: on two 20-claim runs, single-agent coverage was 13 and 12, isolated workers 17 and 16, centralized swarm 19 and 18, and decentralized swarm 18 and 17 (repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md, repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md). This is clear evidence that parallel collective organization improved verified dataset-identifier coverage over one agent. The score stops at 8 because centralized and decentralized arms were effectively tied, the decentralized arm fabricated an identifier on a first attempt in experiment 1, all arms used the same model/provider, n=20 per run is small, costs were roughly 5.2x and 10.7x the single arm, and the metric verifies landing pages rather than whether the proposed datasets scientifically measure each claim; the Aristotle pilot likewise found no swarm accuracy advantage and lacked ground truth (repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md).
justifications.execution-validation: This is a functioning, externally queryable system with claims, proofs, tests, organism records, MCP interfaces and nanopublication manifests, not an architecture sketch (repo/mcp/README.md, captured/nanopub-manifests.txt). The executable-claims snapshot reports 131 reproduced, but also 24 drifted, 6 skipped, 3 failed and 6 unverified runs (repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json), while an independent MCP audit reports 93 of 100 cases passing and identifies concrete defects (captured/github-issues.json issue #56). Validation is therefore substantial but incomplete: 141 of 174 tested claims lack independent faithfulness review, issue #72 records that published nanopubs can drift from result.json, and issue #75 records a failing Lean exposure check (repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md, captured/github-issues.json).
justifications.collaboration-bonus: The pack documents more than an offer: SentiLab reused the HotSpot work, independently reran it, incorporated a patch and credited Delfie in its slides, which is material cross-team propagation (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md). MorphoSwarm Frontier also imported Delphi claims and exposed a live adapter, although its own record says no cross-boundary scientific result had yet been produced; the public MCP and Fittest integration are useful shared infrastructure but are not by themselves evidence of another team's result (repo/COLLABORATIONS.md, repo/plugins/fittest/README.md). This merits a high bonus, but not 10, because the strongest documented reuse is concentrated in one collaboration and the internal forum shows little uptake (captured/forum-feed.json).

problem-significance: Select one current biological question with a named external scientist, explicit decision consequence and matched organism dataset, then make it the headline target instead of treating all 1,763 claims as equally central.
scientific-impact: Complete independent non-builder faithfulness reviews for the highest-impact unchecked tests and remove not-representative results from headline evidence counts.
Replicate a headline biological result on an independent dataset or organism rather than adding another historical or computational claim.
decentralized-agency: Run one end-to-end task where agents independently claim work, revise priorities and hand off through shared state without a human assigning the work packages, then preserve the event log.
collective-capability: Blindly score the existing four-arm outputs for scientific dataset-variable adequacy, not merely resolvable identifiers, using an independent provider and an adjudicated reference.
Repeat with at least two model families so model choice is not confounded with organization.
execution-validation: Resolve or explicitly quarantine the 24 drifted, 3 failed and 6 unverified executable claims and add a release check that compares published nanopub verdicts with current result.json files.
Close the failing Lean exposure and stale static-mirror checks recorded in issue #75.
collaboration-bonus: Obtain a second external team's committed result or report that directly depends on a Delphi tool, dataset or experiment, with a stable link and exact artifact reused.

comparison_found.note: Two pre-registered 20-claim experiments compared single agent, isolated workers, centralized swarm and decentralized swarm on verified dataset-identifier coverage. Collective arms beat the single agent, but centralized and decentralized swarms were indistinguishable; the comparison did not adjudicate scientific adequacy of the datasets and used one model/provider.

top_three_fixes: 1. Add blinded independent scientific-adequacy scoring to the existing four-arm outputs, converting the strongest comparison from URL coverage into a science-relevant benchmark.
2. Run the independent faithfulness gate on the highest-impact unchecked claim tests and revise headline counts to include only representative evidence.
3. Repair the drifted, failed and unverified executable claims and enforce result.json-to-nanopub consistency at release.

highest_value_improvement.title: Blindly adjudicate four-arm scientific adequacy
highest_value_improvement.what: Have a non-builder provider, blind to arm labels, score every proposed dataset in the two existing four-arm experiments against a fixed rubric for whether its variables, population and access route can actually test the assigned claim; adjudicate disagreements and publish arm-level totals beside the existing identifier-coverage totals.
highest_value_improvement.why_this_one: The runs and outputs already exist, so this adds little compute or engineering while directly strengthening the 25%-weight collective-capability criterion and the validation criterion. It is cheaper than running a new swarm experiment or completing faithfulness review across 141 tests, and it addresses the largest weakness in the project's strongest comparative evidence.
highest_value_improvement.evidence_that_would_prove_it: A committed blinded-adjudication table keyed to all 40 claims, with per-dataset variable/population/access verdicts, assessor identities, disagreements, adjudicated arm totals and the unchanged pre-registered arm labels revealed only after scoring.

missing_evidence: Independent domain-expert review of the biological meaning and novelty of the headline data results.
A blinded ground-truth assessment of scientific adequacy for the four-arm comparison outputs.
Complete independent faithfulness assessments for 141 of the 174 tested claims.
Independent replication on a second dataset or organism for the headline biological findings.
Evidence that the decentralized organization outperforms the centralized swarm rather than merely matching it.
summary: Delphi is an unusually substantial and self-critical scientific claim system: it has formal proofs, organism-linked tests, reproducibility records and a real four-arm agent comparison. Its strongest limitation is that much of the scale is not yet biologically validated: most claims remain untested, most completed tests lack independent faithfulness review, and the measured collective advantage is identifier coverage rather than scientific correctness.
